newsitem.title: USA: US outright crudes shed recent gains, grades still.
newsitem.headline: US outright crudes shed recent gains, grades still.

text.p: U.S. outright crude prices shed Friday's gains to end Monday on a down note, while domestic grades were dull with only a few transactions confirmed.

Traders said the combination of a wide swing in outright prices, along with the absence of many traders due to the National Petroleum Refiners Association convention, worked to keep a lid on dealings.
"We had a big flat price move, and a wide range. So, it's hard to say if the NPRA's or the outright move kept the market quiet," said one Texas-based trader.

April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late in the session at $20.85-95 per barrel, around 40 cts lower. Apr/May spreads remained consistent at the 5-7 cts level, keeping the market in backwardation for at least one more session.

Deals confirmed were at a trio of prices for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, with the earliest trades at WTI/Cushing minus 13 and 16 cts, and a later trade at an 11 cts discount. Firmness in the LLS brought the key sweet grade around 5-8 cts stronger than the last deals on Friday.

Traders said they could see no discernible trend for the LLS move to firmer ground, noting the fundamentals are bearish on an intermediate basis, and the opening for bringing over Brent and other foreign crudes was open.
Dated Brent sold at weaker prices, putting the market at April Brent minus 85 cts.
Other trades were in Eugene Island at WTI/Cushing -$2.40, and for West Texas Sour/Midland at -$2.57 to the marker.
Sour prices were slightly firmer but came in slim volume, mostly mopping-up deals, traders said.
